findings.evidence: The criterion is 'bash harness/document-validation/test.sh && python3 .../conformance.py ...'. test.sh itself runs conformance.py internally (harness/document-validation/test.sh:19,51) against the same interface.py the breakage edits, so breaking DIALECT_2020_12 fails test.sh and the '&&' short-circuits before the named conformance.py ever runs. The recorded breakage_output ends 'passed 12, failed 12', which is test.sh's own summary; the expected_failure's 'conformance.py exits 1 ... dropping to 6/28 cases (3 passed per binding, cases_passed=3 each)' is output the chain cannot produce.
findings.fix: Rewrite expected_failure to describe what the chain actually prints (test.sh's failing dialect checks and its 'passed 12, failed 12' line), or make the criterion run conformance.py first so the counts named are observable.

findings.evidence: breakage widens check_edge_type's implementation rule (harness/core-graph/interface.py:113-119), the breakage docs/decomposition.md section 3.1 row C3 names, whose consequence is 'false_accepts becomes non-zero'. expected_failure instead describes a retraction fault: 'That binding now folds to a graph value missing the retracted edge and the record that withdrew it, the two bindings disagree on every structure containing a retraction, verdict_mismatches becomes non-zero'. A widened type rule removes no retraction and makes no binding disagree with the other; 'That binding' has no antecedent because the breakage is not binding-specific. The recorded breakage_output confirms the real signal: 'the widened checker admits the counterexample and the oracle still flags it ... oracle reports false_accepts=1 while the checker reports 0'.
findings.fix: Replace expected_failure with the false_accepts/oracle-mismatch outcome the breakage produces, or move the retraction text to the row whose breakage removes a retraction.

summary: All eight criteria were run once and all eight exit 0; every sourced quote is a verbatim substring of at least one cited record (174/174). The defects are concentrated in the definitions of done. Five skills (core-document, core-graph, core-ledger, seam-state, xc-budget) describe an expected_failure in terms of a standalone conformance.py that the '&&' chain never reaches, because each harness test.sh runs the same conformance internally over the file the breakage edits and fails first. xc-audit-trail's expected and expected_failure both name output its criterion cannot produce - its stated failure signature (independent False, scheduled False) is what the passing gate asserts, and its expected promises entries_checked=100 and adapters_run=2 against a run that prints 24 and 1. core-graph's expected_failure describes a retraction fault its edge-rule breakage cannot cause. xc-compensation's recorded breakage failed to apply at all. xc-budget carries one invented uncited rule (three retries) under a mismatched quote plus a reworded restatement of build-definition-of-done. xc-correlation-implement is clean: its expected, breakage and expected_failure all match the run.
